units.text: `ComposeTestRule` lets you start an activity displaying any composable: your full application, a single screen, or a small element.

quotes.quote: ComposeTestRule lets you start an activity displaying any composable: your full application, a single screen, or a small element.

units.text: It's also a good practice to check that your composables are correctly encapsulated and they work independently, allowing for easier and more focused UI testing.

quotes.quote: It's also a good practice to check that your composables are correctly encapsulated and they work independently, allowing for easier and more focused UI testing

units.text: This doesn't mean you should *only* create unit UI tests. UI tests scoping larger parts of your UI are also very important.

quotes.quote: This doesn't mean you should *only* create unit UI tests. UI tests scoping larger parts of your UI are also very important.

units.text: Oftentimes you need to set the content under test using `composeTestRule.setContent` and you also need to access activity resources, for example to assert that a displayed text matches a string resource. However, you can't call `setContent` on a rule created with `createAndroidComposeRule()` if the activity already calls it.

units.text: A common pattern to achieve this is to create an `AndroidComposeTestRule` using an empty activity such as `ComponentActivity`.

units.text: You should only use custom Semantics properties when it's hard to match a specific item using the given finders and matchers.

quotes.quote: You should only use custom Semantics properties when it's hard to match a specific item using the given finders and matchers.

units.text: Using custom Semantics properties to expose visual properties such as colors, font size or rounded corner radius is not recommended, as it can pollute production code and wrong implementations can lead to bugs that are hard to find.

units.text: Robolectric can also run UI tests such as Espresso or Compose tests. You can convert an instrumented test to Robolectric by moving it to the `test` source set and setting up the Robolectric dependencies.

quotes.quote: Robolectric can also run UI tests such as Espresso or Compose tests. You can convert an instrumented test to Robolectric by moving it to the test source set and setting up the Robolectric dependencies.
android { testOptions { unitTests { isIncludeAndroidResources = true } } }

units.text: Any UI test present in the `test` source set runs with Robolectric.

quotes.quote: Any UI test present in the test source set runs with Robolectric.

units.text: You can run behavior tests on Robolectric as the fidelity needed for it is more than enough. For example, when a Compose test verifies that the UI has changed after clicking a button.

quotes.quote: You can run behavior tests on Robolectric as the fidelity needed for it is more than enough. For example, when a Compose test verifies that the UI has changed after clicking a button.

units.text: You must decide whether Robolectric's implementation is good enough for each use case, but here are some recommendations:

quotes.quote: You must decide whether Robolectric's implementation is good enough for each use case, but here are some recommendations:

units.text: - Use Robolectric for isolated UI behavior tests for components, feature or application tests. In general these tests check the state management and behavior of the UIs and don't interact with external dependencies.

quotes.quote: Use Robolectric for isolated UI behavior tests for components, feature or application tests. In general these tests check the state management and behavior of the UIs and don't interact with external dependencies.

units.text: In summary, Robolectric provides enough fidelity to run most UI tests but some cases will still require device tests, for example those related to system UI like edge-to-edge or picture-in-picture, or when relying on unsupported features, like `WebView`.

quotes.quote: In summary, Robolectric provides enough fidelity to run most UI tests but some cases will still require device tests, for example those related to system UI like edge-to-edge or picture-in-picture, or when relying on unsupported features, like WebView.

units.text: DON'T mock or spy on Android classes that will be acted on by other Android code (e.g. `Context`, `SharedPreferences`, and many others). Stubbing is very brittle and can lead to breakages on Robolectric or Android Platform upgrades. The small exceptions to this rule are classes with very narrow responsibilities, such as event listeners.
